metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Long Branch, PA
metaDescription: Long Branch, Washington County sits in core Marcellus wet-gas territory. Learn how the Washington County courthouse process works for mineral sales.
heroLead: Long Branch is a small Washington County community sitting inside one of the most heavily leased wet-gas Marcellus areas in the entire state.
intro: If your family has land near Long Branch, chances are decent that a landman has already been out at some point in the last fifteen years, because Washington County has seen about as much Marcellus leasing activity as anywhere in Pennsylvania. That history actually helps us evaluate your interest — it usually means there's a real paper trail to work from at the county courthouse rather than a blank slate.

sections.heading: What the Washington County Recorder's Office Shows Us
paragraphs: We pull your deed, any recorded lease, and any unit declaration filed against the parcel at the recorder's office in the county seat. Given how much leasing activity has happened here, it's common to find more than one document in the chain, and we go through each one before discussing value.

Washington County's early and extensive leasing activity means it's not unusual to find a Long Branch parcel that's been under two or three different leases over the years as operators changed hands, and we sort through that history before discussing value.

sections.heading: Why Washington County Set the Pace for the Whole Play
paragraphs: Washington was among the first and most heavily developed counties when Marcellus horizontal drilling took off, and that early, extensive activity still shapes how mineral interests here are evaluated today — there's simply more comparable data available than in less-developed counties.

sections.heading: What Happens After We Review Your Record
paragraphs: Once we've gone through the title and any existing lease or unit, we put together a written range and walk you through exactly how we got there. You decide from there, with no pressure to move faster than you're comfortable with.

faqs.question: I signed a lease years ago and forgot about it — does that matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, an existing lease affects how your interest is valued and structured, so we check for it specifically rather than assuming your minerals are unleased.

faqs.question: Why is Washington County considered such a strong Marcellus area?
faqs.answer: It was one of the earliest and most extensively developed counties in the play, with a long track record of production and leasing activity.

faqs.question: How do I get started?
faqs.answer: Send us your parcel information or deed if you have it, and we'll pull the rest of the record from the county courthouse.

faqs.question: What if my Long Branch deed references an old road that no longer exists?
faqs.answer: That's common in older Washington County descriptions — we cross-reference historical plat maps with current tax parcel data to confirm exactly which tract the deed describes.
